title: Solving Differential Equations Using Continuous-Variable Quantum Annealing
authors: Kazuki Miyanishi, Soshun Naito, Asuka Koura, Kazue Kudo, Toshiki Yamaji, Yuichiro Matsuzaki
abstract: Most existing quantum annealing approaches are formulated for qubit-based architectures. Consequently, applying them to continuous-variable optimization problems requires discretizing the variables, which can incur substantial qubit overhead. Continuous-variable quantum annealing based on bosonic systems has recently been proposed as an alternative framework, in which each optimization variable is directly encoded in a bosonic mode, such as a cavity mode. In this work, we develop a continuous-variable quantum annealing formulation for solving linear differential equations. By recasting the determination of the solution as a continuous-variable optimization problem, the differential equation can be mapped onto an objective function compatible with bosonic quantum annealing. Numerical simulations of second-order linear differential equations demonstrate that, under the conditions considered, the proposed formulation reproduces the corresponding analytical solutions. These results establish a potential route toward solving differential equations without the discretization overhead inherent in qubit-based implementations.
summary: The authors propose a novel method to solve linear ordinary differential equations by reformulating the problem as a continuous-variable optimization task suitable for bosonic quantum annealing. By mapping this objective function onto a specific Hamiltonian, they demonstrate that their approach successfully reproduces known analytical solutions in numerical tests. This work offers a promising route to solving complex physical problems without resorting to variable discretization overhead.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop a quantum annealing approach capable of solving linear ordinary differential equations (ODEs) without the computational overhead associated with discretizing variables for qubit-based systems.
main_result: Numerical simulations successfully demonstrated that the proposed continuous-variable formulation can reproduce known analytical solutions for second-order linear ODEs, establishing a viable pathway for this application.
method: The ODE solution is recast as a continuous-variable optimization problem whose objective function is then mapped onto a bosonic Hamiltonian suitable for continuous-variable quantum annealing (CVQA).
model_or_system: The model utilizes bosonic systems, such as cavity modes, where each optimization variable is directly encoded in a bosonic mode. The formulation relies on approximating derivatives using central finite differences.

paper_structure: The paper first establishes the motivation by contrasting CVQA with qubit-based methods. It then details the mathematical formulation, mapping the discretized ODE into a quadratic cost function and subsequently deriving the bosonic Hamiltonian $\hat{H}_P$. Finally, it presents numerical simulations on specific second-order ODEs to validate the approach.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses how quantum computation can tackle continuous physical problems (like solving differential equations) using hardware platforms naturally suited for continuous variables (bosonic systems), bypassing major limitations of current qubit architectures.
